title: Differencing the Diffusion Trajectory toward Uncertain Components for Time Series Forecasting
claim: A single diffusion process can embed predictability asymmetry by progressively shifting targets toward differenced structure, conditioned on gated value and difference history.
layout: Top trajectory strip plus bottom denoiser module, left-to-right, formulas in corner boxes
description: A wide architecture diagram with two stacked parts. The top shows a clean time-series window x0, split into a yellow-shaded history/label region and a future region. Dash-dotted arrows lead from it to a row of four noisy series panels (T, t, s, and a final panel). The noise gradually decreases, and pink uncertainty bands appear along the way. Curved solid arrows between panels mark the reverse steps. Gray rounded boxes at the corners hold the reverse-process update equations and the forward distribution q(x_t|x_0). The bottom shows the conditional denoiser on a pale blue background. The value-domain history and its differenced version feed two MLPs. Mean, Concat and sigmoid blocks produce a gate g. The gate multiplies h_diff, then the result is added to h_val to give c. This goes with x_t and t into the h_theta block. Linear heads output mu-hat and v-hat. A legend in the bottom right explains the arrow and operator symbols.
caption: Overall architecture of DiffDiff. Top: the differencing forward process gradually shifts the clean target $x_0$ toward its differenced structure under the step-dependent operator $A_t$, and the deterministic reverse step recovers $x_s$ from the denoiser prediction $\hat{x}_0$. Bottom: the stage-adaptive conditional denoiser encodes both the value-domain history $x_{hist}$ and its first-order differences $\Deltax_{hist}$, fuses them through a sigmoid gate conditioned on the diffusion timestep, and outputs the value-domain prediction along with auxiliary statistics for instance denormalization.
abstract: Diffusion models have become a widely used framework for probabilistic time series forecasting, modeling the distribution of future values given an observed history. In time series forecasting, however, the future continues the observed history, creating an asymmetry the standard diffusion process leaves unaddressed, with slowly-varying content largely determined by the observed continuity while higher-frequency dynamics carry most of the residual uncertainty. Existing diffusion-based forecasters decouple this asymmetry through an external rule before generation, leaving the corruption trajectory blind to which parts of the target the history can already anchor. We propose DiffDiff, a diffusion framework that embeds this predictability asymmetry into the diffusion trajectory itself, so that a single end-to-end diffusion process becomes aware of which parts of the target the history can already anchor. DiffDiff makes the forward operator step-dependent so that the noisy intermediate state progressively shifts from the target itself toward its second-order differenced structure, while a conditioning pathway supplies the denoiser with both value-domain and differential history information balanced by a stage-adaptive gate at each diffusion step. The terminal distribution approaches a standard Gaussian, preserving compatibility with existing samplers. On seven benchmarks across four prediction horizons, DiffDiff outperforms six diffusion baselines, while our analyses show that its trajectory reallocates modeling effort according to history predictability and improves distributional fidelity.
